docs(plan): step 11 done; the interactive archetype decided; WCAG and 360 px as platform rules

## Intent

Close the explainer step with the lessons of the first full run, and take on the interactive archetype before the evals. Interactive apps are free in their architecture, so a shared, minimal architecture frame should guide the agent early. Accessibility has limits in such apps: WCAG and 360 px bind the platform, while a single app may deviate and say so.

## Key changes

- The plan marks step 11 done with the lessons of the Elektrizität run, records the tutor as brought forward against Q5, and puts the interactive archetype (12) before the evals (10).
- The plan holds the decided sketch of the interactive archetype: one archetype with recipes in the skill; Vue with TypeScript, free in decomposition, data, logic and rendering; a minimal shell (start page, app page, languages, storage, hash routes); core, view, data and playthroughs.
- Each interactive app carries an arc42 architecture in English and minimal: a frame from the tooling that lernapps update replaces, and the app's own part. arc42 diff runs before a commit; the code is not checked against responsibilities.
- Small storage is localStorage through the existing wrapper, with a quota per app. A wrapper for IndexedDB comes only when an app needs it.
- Accessibility limits go into an optional field of the catalog entry. Low stimulation is advice in the skill, not a duty.
- The constraints of the tooling's architecture: WCAG 2.1 AA and 360 px are rules of the platform; apps meet them by default and may deviate where their idea needs it, saying so in their entry.

## Dependencies and side effects

- lernapps/.github states the same rule in ORGANIZATION.md and CONTRIBUTING.md (199fecc).
- Skills and checks still ask every app for WCAG and 360 px until the entry field and its checks exist.

docs: WCAG 2.1 AA and 360 px are rules of the platform; apps may deviate and say so

## Intent

Accessibility has its limits in some apps, for example a fast typing game. The platform itself must always be accessible, while a single app may deviate where its idea needs it.

## Key changes

- Pages of the platform (the site frame, the catalog and the overview pages) meet WCAG 2.1 AA, are usable at 360 px and are readable without JavaScript.
- Apps meet WCAG 2.1 AA and are usable at 360 px by default. An app may deviate and says so in its entry.

## Dependencies and side effects

- The tooling's plan and architecture state the same rule (tooling#87, same intent).
